criteria.rationale: The socket-bound cause is addressed, but the assumption that the random suffix is always 10 digits is false.
The exclusive claim precedes directory creation and os.Mkdir is exclusive; the race left affects only which refusal is returned (N17).
No record, brief or adapter command changes.
The attempt id is matched by a strict pattern; existing paths and links are refused.
Resume and handoff both consult the check; task runs do not use this function. Focused continuity and handoff tests passed locally with a private XDG_STATE_HOME.
Failures name the directory and the reason in the error or run record.
Earlier records keep their meaning; the transitional gap for resuming older runs is N18.
The cause was a random path removed by cleanup; a per-attempt path recreates it (D1). The design assessment observed no structural delta, so no mapping is owed.
Both manuals state the stable path, TMPDIR condition and remedy, matching the code; the pt-BR scaffold copy is identical and the English copy differs only by the contributor-mode block.
Refusals name the path and a remedy; the wording gap is N19.
R1 and R2 are exercised by the resume test, R3 by the exclusivity and resume tests; the exclusivity test's flakiness is N16.
The change stays in the runtime directory, its two continuation checks, tests and manuals.
Mode 0700, exclusive creation, no link following, cleanup identity checks unchanged; predictability falls within L2 and L3, which I found justified.
A stable name is smaller than changing the sealed brief to announce a new path; it would be invalid if one attempt could have two live runs.

findings.action: The R3 test is flaky and breaks the unit gate: it requires the attempt name to be no longer than one random os.MkdirTemp name, but that suffix is a uint32 in decimal (1 to 10 digits), so shorter draws fail it. Measured 235 failures in 1000 runs; it also failed in a plain -run RunContinuity run. The comment at review_dispatch.go:2038 ('as long as the random suffix') carries the same wrong assumption. Compare against the longest random name (prefix plus 10 digits) instead of a sample.
Make the continuation claim and the runtime-directory check one step, or re-read the claim before refusing
findings.rationale: Carries R2-N8 and R3-N12: the claim lookup and the directory check are not atomic, so a resume or handoff that loses a race can get the directory refusal instead of pending. Established by reading.

findings.action: Refuse or warn on resume when the predecessor's safety.runtime_id differs from the attempt's path
findings.rationale: Carries R3-N11: a run interrupted under an earlier engine used a random runtime directory; resuming it creates the stable path without telling the session, which still points at the removed checkout. The predecessor's safety.runtime_id is never compared. Transitional.

findings.action: Word the remedy neutrally, such as 'then run again'
findings.rationale: Carries R3-N13: PlanReviewHandoff returns a refusal ending in 'then resume' although the operator asked for a handoff.

findings.action: Skip only the link case when os.Symlink is not permitted
findings.rationale: Carries R3-N14: an os.Symlink error is fatal, so the test fails on Windows without the symlink privilege instead of skipping the link case.

findings.action: Decide in a follow-up spec whether continued rounds need a stable path or a path notice
findings.rationale: Carries R3-N15: a session continued into a new round belongs to a new attempt, so its checkout path differs from the one the session saw. Outside this spec's resume scope; established by reading.
